messages:
maria: heads up — deploybot bumped a release for the infra-config PR (auto-bump enabled). It created v1.8.6+cfg20260320 instead of v1.8.7. Is that what we want?

devin: I saw that. The bot's current rule is: config-only -> append +cfg<date>, code/behavior -> increment patch.

alex: I'd prefer an actual patch bump for anything that ends up in releases/ and gets released to customers. Buildmeta gets ignored by some package managers and by git-based rollbacks.

maria: true — but for our semver doc we also said non-behavioral ops changes shouldn't move public semver if they don't affect APIs. The +build approach preserves that intent.

releasebot: deploybot: created tag v1.8.6+cfg20260320 for PR #4721 (infra: routing defaults). Canary scheduled: 02:30 UTC.

sam: quick question — if we keep +buildmeta, does the release notes generator pick those up as new releases? We don't want noisy release notes for tiny knobs.

devin: rn-gen currently treats tags with buildmeta as releases but marks them as "meta" and collapses them under same patch in the changelog. It will only create a visible entry if the PR has user-facing labels.

alex: that behavior is okay, but the problem is our rollback playbook which expects to `git checkout v1.8.6` to reproduce. Buildmeta makes that ambiguous, since some deploy snapshots strip +meta. I've seen ops confusion during a rollback once.

maria: proposal: change deploybot rule to prefer patch bump when any of these are true: PR touches src/ or lib/, PR label includes user-impact, or changelog labels are present. Otherwise use +cfg<yyyymmdd>. That keeps deploys tidy and avoids accidental public bumps.

devin: I can implement that. Edge cases: terraform-only changes that change infra behavior (routing) — they might be user-impacting even if files are infra. We should add an override label like "force-patch" to be explicit.

sam: add "force-patch" is fine. Also let's document the tagging examples so oncall knows how to interpret them. Small snippet: `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[+meta]` where meta can be `cfgYYYYMMDD` or `canaryNN` or `buildHASH`.

sre-bot: reminder: rollback playbook snippet for tagging: `git tag -l 'v*' --points-at <commit>` then use explicit tag resolution. If tag contains +meta, use full tag string when checking out.

alex: agree with the label/override approach. Also let's add a rule in change windows: between 22:00-06:00 UTC only emergency patches allowed (and they must be force-patch + release note). Deploybot should refuse auto-patch outside window unless `force-patch` present.

maria: ok I'll open a tiny RFC to update docs + deploybot rules. Devin can take the bot change after that. Action items: maria -> RFC, devin -> PR for deploybot rule and add `force-patch`, sam -> update release notes generator docs, alex -> update rollback playbook lines about +meta.

devin: noted. I'll also add a short test in deploybot: simulate tagging: `v1.8.6+cfg20260320` vs `v1.8.7` and assert behavior.

maria: thanks — let's sync tomorrow if anything ambiguous comes up. :thumbsup:
